title: CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts and styles
description: Content-Security-Policy header includes 'unsafe-inline' for both script-src and style-src directives, weakening XSS mitigation.
risks: Enables XSS attacks by allowing inline script/style injection if other input vectors exist.
attack_vectors: If any input reflection or DOM-based XSS sink exists, unsafe-inline allows attacker scripts to execute within CSP policy.
remediation: Replace unsafe-inline with nonce-based or hash-based CSP directives for scripts and styles.

title: Server version disclosure in HTTP headers
description: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) version disclosed in Server header on all HTTP responses including error pages.
risks: Attackers can target known nginx 1.24.0 vulnerabilities and Ubuntu-specific issues more precisely.
attack_vectors: Use disclosed version to search for specific nginx 1.24.0 or Ubuntu package CVEs and craft targeted exploits.
proof_of_existence: Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) — present in all responses including 403 and 405 error pages.
remediation: Set server_tokens off in nginx configuration to suppress version information.

title: Sensitive dotfiles probed — 403 Forbidden (blocked)
description: .git/HEAD, .git/config, and .env all return 403 Forbidden — nginx blocks access to dotfiles but their existence is unconfirmed.
risks: No direct risk — access is blocked. If misconfiguration occurs, these files could leak source code or secrets.
attack_vectors: No current exploit path. Could attempt bypass via path traversal, encoding, or alternate case if nginx config changes.
proof_of_existence: GET /.git/HEAD → 403 Forbidden (nginx/1.24.0). GET /.env → 403 Forbidden. GET /.git/config → 403 Forbidden.
remediation: Maintain nginx dotfile blocking; verify files don't exist in webroot; add explicit deny rules.

title: No CMS backend detected — custom static site
description: /blog/ returns custom static HTML (not WordPress, Ghost, or any CMS). /blog/wp-login.php and /blog/ghost/ both return 404.
risks: Reduced attack surface — no CMS-specific vulnerabilities apply (e.g., no wp-admin brute force, no plugin exploits).
attack_vectors: No CMS exploitation paths available. Static site limits server-side attack surface.
proof_of_existence: GET /blog/wp-login.php → 404. GET /blog/ghost/ → 404. GET /blog/ → 200 with static HTML, no CMS signatures.
remediation: N/A — static site is inherently more secure than CMS-based sites.

title: HTTP methods restricted to GET/HEAD only
description: OPTIONS and TRACE methods return 405 Not Allowed. No verb tampering or XST attack surface.
risks: No risk — properly restricted HTTP methods reduce attack surface.
attack_vectors: No available method-based attacks. PUT/DELETE not tested but likely also restricted.
poc: curl -sk -X OPTIONS https://cyberian-defenses.com/ -D -; curl -sk -X TRACE https://cyberian-defenses.com/ -D -
proof_of_existence: OPTIONS → 405 Not Allowed. TRACE → 405 Not Allowed. Both return proper error with security headers.
remediation: N/A — correctly configured. Consider testing PUT/DELETE/PATCH methods for completeness.

title: searchsploit tool non-functional — exploit DB unavailable
description: searchsploit commands for nginx 1.24 and OpenSSH 9.6 both failed with rc_file configuration error.
risks: Inability to search for known CVEs/exploits for detected service versions limits vulnerability research.
attack_vectors: N/A — tooling limitation. Manual CVE research via NVD/MITRE recommended as alternative.
proof_of_existence: [!] Could not find: rc_file ~ — both searchsploit invocations failed with exit code 1.
remediation: Fix searchsploit configuration or use online exploit-db.com and NVD for manual CVE lookups.

title: robots.txt and sitemap.xml publicly accessible — site structure exposed
description: robots.txt allows all crawlers and references sitemap.xml listing index.html, services.html, about.html and likely more pages.
risks: Attacker can enumerate all site pages from sitemap.xml without brute-forcing directories.
attack_vectors: Fetch robots.txt and sitemap.xml to map all public endpoints, then test each for vulnerabilities.
proof_of_existence: robots.txt: User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https://cyberian-defenses.com/sitemap.xml. sitemap.xml lists index.html, services.html, about.html...
remediation: Consider restricting robots.txt if non-public pages are listed; ensure sitemap only contains intended public pages.

title: No .well-known/security.txt — vulnerability disclosure policy missing
description: GET /.well-known/security.txt returns 403 Forbidden — no security contact or disclosure policy published.
risks: Security researchers cannot find responsible disclosure contact; may publish vulnerabilities without coordination.
attack_vectors: N/A — informational. Lack of security.txt may lead to uncoordinated vulnerability disclosure.
proof_of_existence: GET /.well-known/security.txt → 403 Forbidden (nginx/1.24.0 Ubuntu). No security.txt file served.
remediation: Create and publish /.well-known/security.txt with security contact, encryption key, and disclosure policy.
